title: Collapsible Insights: multi-metric cost snapshot — visual polish & feedback loop
creator: Avery Chen
description: Deliver a compact, collapsible 'Insights' module for the Console that surfaces multiple cost/time-series metrics in a single snapshot card. This ticket captures the visual-polish pass after initial prototype testing: redlines, accessibility checks, and a prioritized list of developer handoff artifacts. Goal is to reduce visual noise while preserving scanability for engineers and finance stakeholders.
background: The current cost tiles occupy too much vertical space when teams run many dashboards. Engineering asked for a space-efficient card that can expand to show per-model charts and contract to a one-line summary. Prior prototypes (see links) validated the concept but flagged visibility and keyboard navigation issues. This work consolidates feedback from Product, Analytics, and SRE and prepares for design->eng handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Collapsed state shows primary metric, relative delta, and a micro-sparkline
Expanded state reveals up to 3 mini time-series with labels and toggles
Contrast meets WCAG AA for text and trend lines at both densities
Component accessible via keyboard and screen-readers; announce expanded state
Dev acceptance: Figma tokens and CSS variables provided; interactions documented
QA checklist completed for zero-data state, high-card-count grids, and mobile widths
comments: 2025-02-19 - Product (Jordan Mills): Liked compact state; ask to surface 'top contributing model' as a badge in expanded view.
2025-02-20 - Eng (Priya Nair): Concern about reflow cost when expanding dozens of cards on the page; proposal to virtualize expanded content. Added ENG-40211 as dependency.
2025-02-21 - Design review (Avery Chen): Redlines attached — increase micro-sparkline stroke to 2px at small sizes, swap amber delta to neutral gray for values <1% change.

2025-02-22 - Accessibility (Sam Ortega): Keyboard focus needs a clear ring and 'Enter' toggles expand/collapse; screen-reader should read "Card title, collapsed, press enter to expand". Added specific aria-labels to spec.
2025-02-23 - QA (Lina Gomez): Edge case: when metrics are all zero, card collapses visually; recommend showing 'No data' micro-copy and a thin placeholder sparkline. QA will own regression test case.
2025-02-24 - Stakeholder (Ben Holt, Analytics): Request that export CSV link be available in expanded toolbar; PM flagged as follow-up (PM-884).

2025-02-25 - Handoff notes (Riley Patel): Figma component tokens exported; preparing dev ticket with CSS variables and interaction map. Devs requested a compact token set — trimmed from 12 to 6 spacing tokens.
2025-02-26 - Visual polish pass (Avery Chen): Finalized color tweaks and microcopy edits; removed iconography in collapsed state to reduce noise per research feedback.
2025-02-27 - Design sign-off (Product Lead Maya Singh): Approved visual direction pending ENG acceptance and accessibility checklist completion.
redlines: Increase hit target for expand chevron to 40px square
Line height for metric label set to 16px at small sizes
Ensure 12px gap between sparkline and delta badge in collapsed state
Use token --color-graph-1 for primary series, --color-graph-2 for secondary with 60% opacity for comparison lines
qa_tasks: Add regression test for grid with 50 cards and randomized expand/collapse
Verify keyboard nav: tab to card -> enter expands -> esc collapses
Contrast tests on 3 most common themes (light/dark/high-contrast)
Zero-data microcopy presence and export CSV function in expanded toolbar
dev_handoff_items: Figma component library link and variant table
Interaction map (hover, focus, expand/collapse, export) as plain HTML snippets
CSS tokens: spacing, radii, typography, colors (provided)
Acceptance criteria and QA checklist included in ticket description
next_steps: Eng to evaluate virtualization approach for expansion (ENG-40211)
PM to confirm CSV export scope for MVP (PM-884)
Design to produce a micro-interaction spec for chevron motion and collapse animation
Schedule a 30-min dev design review the week of 2025-03-03
